title: One Point Lesson - Hydrogen Reduction Safety & Exotherm Control (OPL-DC-3401A-04)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-DC-3401A-04 - Hydrogen Reduction Safety & Exotherm Control.

Equipment: DC-3401A (CATALYST REDUCTION REACTOR), Discipline: Process / Operations, Area: 3400 - CATALYST REDUCTION SYSTEM.

Related Interlock: SEQ-3401 (SIL 2), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-3401.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains hydrogen reduction safety & exotherm control for DC-3401A in the CATALYST REDUCTION SYSTEM. Hydrogen is flammable over 4-75 % in air. During reduction the PdO->Pd reaction is exothermic and the bed temperature must be watched closely.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: Obtain the correct operating permit and brief the shift team before the task.
- Precaution 2: Confirm hazardous fluids are isolated / inerted as required by procedure.
- Precaution 3: Beware of flammable, hot, or high-pressure fluids; wear the correct PPE.
- Precaution 4: Never defeat a safety interlock or trip without an authorised override permit.
- Precaution 5: Have emergency actions and communications ready before starting.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: Operating procedure & P&ID
- Tool 2: Radio / communication with panel
- Tool 3: Gas detector (O2 / LEL) as required
- Tool 4: Correct PPE for the fluid handled
- Tool 5: Sample containers & PPE for sampling
- Tool 6: Permit-to-work documentation

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Introduce H2 only after inerting and bed homogeneity are confirmed
- Step 1 - Check: Permit valid & briefed
- Step 2 - Action: Hold a constant N2+H2 flow for about 12 hours
- Step 2 - Check: Parameter within limit
- Step 3 - Action: Watch TE-3401 for any exotherm approaching the TSHH-3401 limit
- Step 3 - Check: Interlock status confirmed
- Step 4 - Action: If bed exceeds 230 degC the logic auto-trips heater and blocks H2
- Step 4 - Check: Change logged on DCS
- Step 5 - Action: Keep the reactor vent path (PV-3404) available at all times
- Step 5 - Check: Handover to next shift

COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- Symptom: Bed multipoint TC point 3 reading open circuit | Likely Cause: Thermocouple element failed at the sheath junction | Action: Replaced TC point 3 in the multipoint assembly, verified reading.
- Symptom: One heater bank drawing no current, slow heat-up | Likely Cause: Electric heater element bank open circuit / element burnt | Action: Replaced heater element bank, meggered, verified TIC-17343 response
- Symptom: Inerting O2 analyzer drift vs portable reference | Likely Cause: Analyzer zero drift and sample dryer saturated | Action: Recalibrated AI-3401 on span gas, replaced sample dryer

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: Hydrogen is flammable over 4-75 % in air. During reduction the PdO->Pd reaction is exothermic and the bed temperature must be watched closely.
- Point 2: Respect the interlock SEQ-3401: e.g. TSHH-3401 trips at > 230 degC - never defeat it without a permit.
- Point 3: Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-3401 before working on DC-3401A.
- Point 4: Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.
